markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (51%)** · Ambiguous: InSitu vs Invasive · Careful review
InSitu is close behind at 43%, and both are in the 90% conformal set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 51%, InSitu 43% | Narrow margin |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.92 / 76th percentile | Input looks usable |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 Invasive | Mixed neighbors [F5] |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 0, 3, 10) · ↑ invasive · Above-typical score; concept model links it to invasive [F2] · Validated
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 0, 2, 3) · ↓ invasive · High score; associated with lower invasive likelihood · Unreliable
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 5) · ↓ invasive · Near-typical here; in situ neighbor BACH_0155 scored higher · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 9) · ↑ invasive · Below-typical score; lack of it nudges concept model toward invasive · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions cuts the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (-0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Invasive leads by 8 points; InSitu is nearly as likely.
- Regions 0–3 score low invasive risk (≤16%); signal comes mainly from regions 8–10.

## Check on the slide
1. **8, 9, 10** — highest invasive contribution; look for stromal infiltration versus duct-confined tumor.
2. **5** — strongest nuclear pleomorphism region; compare atypia against in situ appearance.
3. **0, 3** — top regions for infiltrating-stroma score yet low risk; confirm stroma is tumor-infiltrated.
